tools.name: get_net_worth
tools.description: Total net worth: everything owned minus everything owed, plus the breakdown by account. Use for 'what am I worth', 'how much do I have', 'what's my net worth'.

tools.name: get_accounts
tools.description: Every account with its type, value and the holdings inside it. Use for questions about a specific account, provider, or what someone actually holds.

tools.name: get_tax_allowances
tools.description: This tax year's UK allowance usage: ISA, LISA, Junior ISA, pension annual allowance, capital gains and dividends - used, remaining, and the deadline. Use for 'how much ISA allowance do I have left', 'am I close to my CGT exemption'.

tools.name: get_budget
tools.description: Monthly take-home, the bills, debt payments (from Liabilities) and regular saving (from Assets) that come off it, what's free each month, the planned savings rate, where the bills go by category, bills renewing soon, how many months of bills and debt payments the liquid savings would cover, and plan

tools.name: get_net_worth_history
tools.description: Recorded net worth snapshots, oldest first, for questions about change over time.

tools.name: get_goals
tools.description: Every savings goal with its target, target year, what is behind it today, and whether it is on track. Use for 'am I on track', 'will I hit my deposit', 'how are my goals doing'.

tools.name: get_journal
tools.description: Entries from the Journal - what was written down at the time about a decision, and why. Use for 'what did I say when I bought this', 'what was I thinking in March', or any question about past reasoning rather than past numbers.

tools.name: get_holdings
tools.description: Every individual holding across all accounts, largest first, with what it is worth and which account it sits in. Use for questions about a specific fund, share or ticker, or about concentration - 'how much of me is in one thing'.

tools.name: get_performance
tools.description: How net worth has moved over a period, from the daily snapshot history. Use for 'how have I done this year', 'am I up or down', 'what has changed since January'.

tools.name: get_change_explanation
tools.description: Breaks a change in net worth down - money put in against everything else, then account by account where each account's figures were saved (by account type before) - so the answer is not just 'up £4,000' but where it came from. Use whenever someone asks WHY a number moved, or 'what changed this month

tools.name: get_attention
tools.description: Checks that would otherwise only be noticed if someone thought to look: tax allowances about to expire unused, goals that have gone off track, a short cash runway, a savings fix ending and bills renewing or deals ending in the next 30 days. Use for 'anything I should know', 'am I missing anything',

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Makes one of Foliopeak's reports from the person's own figures and gives a short summary and the link to open it, ready to read or save as a PDF: monthly (the Monthly Review), own-owe (every account and debt with their share - for a mortgage, a solicitor or probate), accountant (a limited company di

tools.name: get_retirement_change
tools.description: The earliest age the person could retire with their money lasting to 100 after tax - the Retirement page's Can You Stop sums - today and at the start of the month, then each pension and savings account that moved it and the figures it rests on (payments in, spending, growth), each with a link to see

tools.name: get_retirement_projection
tools.description: Runs a Monte Carlo retirement simulation against the real pot, and reports how often it lasts. Use for 'will my pension last', 'can I retire at 60', 'what if I put more in'. Nothing is saved - this is a calculation, not a change.

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description: Everything in the person's Foliopeak notification bell, in the same words: balances not updated in a while, gaps in their figures (a missing interest rate, birth year or price), goals behind, dates coming up and changes waiting for their approval. Each line says which fix, if any, can be proposed an

tools.name: get_household
tools.description: The household this person shares with a partner: combined net worth, each member's own figure, and the tax-year allowances added together - two ISA allowances, two pension allowances, each child's Junior ISA counted once. Use for 'how much ISA room do we have between us', 'what are we worth together

tools.name: get_since_last_asked
tools.description: A catch-up since the last question through Cairn: how long ago that was, what net worth did in between and why, anything worth knowing right now, and the days to 5 April. Use at the start of a conversation, or for 'what's changed since we last spoke', 'catch me up'.

tools.name: get_cairn_history
tools.description: The record of what has been looked up through Cairn - which tool, when, and whether by an assistant or by the person on the Cairn page. Use for 'what did I ask about in June', 'what has been read from my account'. Kept for twelve months.

tools.name: get_dividends
tools.description: The dividends recorded on Assets: this tax year so far, and how much of that is in general investment accounts against the dividend allowance; the last 12 months by holding; an estimate for the next 12 months; and the most recent payments. Use for 'how much have I had in dividends', 'which holding p

tools.name: get_resilience
tools.description: Three checks on how much of this position would still stand if one thing went wrong: how many months of bills and debt payments the reachable cash would cover, the single biggest holding's share of the invested money, and unsecured debt against what could be reached. The same checks as the first thr

tools.name: get_wealth_shape
tools.description: Net worth split by how quickly it could actually be reached: accessible cash, invested money (reachable but only by selling), property equity, and pensions (reached at a birthday) - plus how many months of bills and debt payments the accessible cash alone would cover. The same figures as the 'What y

tools.name: get_liabilities
tools.description: Every debt with its balance, rate, monthly payment, the month it clears and the interest still to pay, then the debt-free date at today's payments and what paying a bit more would change, and the dates coming up (a fixed rate ending, a 0% deal ending, a term's end). The same plan as the Liabilities

tools.name: get_business
tools.description: The Business section: what the business holds and owes, the latest figures read in from the accounts or an Etsy, eBay or Shopify sales file (sales, costs, profit, cash) against the period before, tax set aside this tax year, and the next tax dates - Self Assessment, Corporation Tax per company, Maki

tools.name: get_capital_gains
tools.description: The Capital gains tab: this tax year's disposals in general investment and crypto accounts, matched in HMRC's order (same day, 30 days, the pool), the gain after losses, what's left of the annual exempt amount, and whether it's likely to need reporting. Use for 'how much of my CGT allowance have I u

tools.name: get_monthly_review
tools.description: The Monthly review: net worth now, the change on a month and a year ago and what the month's change was made of, ISA allowance left and days to 5 April, goals on track or behind, trades in the last 30 days, and the balances kept by hand not updated this month. The same figures as the Monthly review

tools.name: calculate_take_home
tools.description: UK take-home pay from a salary: income tax, National Insurance, student loan and pension, at this tax year's rates. Use for 'what would I take home on £60k'.

tools.name: calculate_stamp_duty
tools.description: Stamp Duty Land Tax on a home purchase in England or Northern Ireland, at current rates. Use for 'how much stamp duty on £450k'.

tools.name: calculate_capital_gains_tax
tools.description: UK Capital Gains Tax on gains made this tax year, after the annual exemption, at the rate set by the person's income. Use for 'how much CGT would I pay on a £15k gain'.

tools.name: calculate_pension_tax_relief
tools.description: Tax relief on a personal pension contribution paid from taxed pay (relief at source, e.g. a SIPP): what the provider adds, and any extra a higher-rate taxpayer can claim back. Use for 'what relief do I get if I put £8,000 in my SIPP'.

tools.name: calculate_child_benefit_charge
tools.description: How much Child Benefit is clawed back through the High Income Child Benefit Charge at a given adjusted net income, and what is kept. Use for 'do I lose child benefit on £65k', 'how much of the child benefit do we keep'.

tools.name: calculate_adjusted_net_income
tools.description: Adjusted net income from salary, other income, pension contributions and Gift Aid: how much personal allowance is lost above £100,000, what that costs, any Child Benefit charge, and the true marginal rate on the next pound. Use for 'am I in the £100k trap', 'what does earning £110k really cost me'.

tools.name: calculate_marriage_allowance
tools.description: Whether a married couple or civil partners can use Marriage Allowance and what it saves: the lower earner transfers part of their personal allowance to the higher earner. Use for 'can we claim marriage allowance'.

tools.name: calculate_salary_sacrifice
tools.description: What sacrificing part of a salary into a pension does: take-home, Child Benefit charge, what lands in the pension, and the sacrifice that would bring income exactly under £100,000, under the Child Benefit charge, or out of higher-rate tax. Use for 'what would sacrificing £5k save me'.

tools.name: calculate_inheritance_tax
tools.description: An inheritance tax estimate on an estate: nil-rate band, residence nil-rate band, a late spouse's transferred allowances, the charity rate, and the rule from 6 April 2027 that brings unused pensions into the estate. Use for 'how much inheritance tax would be due on our estate'.

tools.name: calculate_pension_inheritance_2027
tools.description: What the April 2027 change does to a pension left behind: inheritance tax with the pension outside the estate (the rules before 6 April 2027) and inside it (from then on), the beneficiary's income tax, and what reaches them. Use for 'what happens to my pension when I die from 2027'.

tools.name: calculate_fire
tools.description: The FIRE number from annual spending and a withdrawal rate, and how many years of saving at a growth rate after inflation reach it, in today's money. Anything not given starts from the person's own figures, as the FIRE page does: the money they could reach before pension age, their saving, their spe

tools.name: calculate_coast_fire
tools.description: Whether what is invested today would grow to the retirement pot on its own, and if not, the age at which contributions could stop. Use for 'have I hit coast FIRE', 'when could I stop paying in'.

tools.name: calculate_debt_payoff
tools.description: How long a set of debts takes to clear and what interest it costs, paying minimums plus an extra amount each month, by avalanche (highest rate first) or snowball (smallest balance first). Use for 'when would we be debt-free', 'avalanche or snowball'.

tools.name: calculate_mortgage_overpayment
tools.description: What a monthly overpayment does to a mortgage: months and interest saved. Use for 'what if I overpaid £200 a month'.

tools.name: calculate_isa_vs_gia
tools.description: The same lump sum in an ISA and in a taxable general investment account over some years: the tax the GIA pays on dividends and gains, and the ISA's advantage. Use for 'is it worth using my ISA for this'.

tools.name: calculate_pension_vs_isa
tools.description: Where a gross amount does more good - pension, ISA or Lifetime ISA - given the marginal rate now, the expected rate in retirement, growth and years, compared per pound of take-home given up. Use for 'pension or ISA for this £5,000'.

tools.name: calculate_student_loan
tools.description: Whether a student loan is likely to be repaid or written off, what it costs over the term, and whether a voluntary overpayment helps. The balance and inflation start from the person's own figures when not given. Use for 'should I overpay my student loan', 'will my plan 2 loan be written off'.

tools.name: calculate_savings_interest_tax
tools.description: Tax due on savings interest given other income: the starting rate for savings, the Personal Savings Allowance, and any spare personal allowance. Use for 'will I pay tax on £1,500 of interest'.

tools.name: calculate_devolved_property_tax
tools.description: Land and Buildings Transaction Tax (Scotland) or Land Transaction Tax (Wales) on a home purchase. Use for 'how much LBTT on £300k in Edinburgh'. Not England or Northern Ireland, which have Stamp Duty.

tools.name: calculate_pension_carry_forward
tools.description: How much unused pension annual allowance from the last three tax years can be carried forward, and the total available this year. Use for 'how much can I put in my pension this year using carry forward'.

tools.name: calculate_required_return
tools.description: The annual growth rate needed for a current pot plus monthly contributions to reach a target by a date. Use for 'what return do I need to hit £500k in 15 years'.

tools.name: calculate_rent_vs_buy
tools.description: Buying a home against renting and investing the difference, over a number of years: when buying pulls ahead, if it does. Use for 'are we better off buying at £350k or renting at £1,400 a month'.

tools.name: calculate_house_equity
tools.description: How equity in a home builds over the mortgage term from repayments, price growth and any overpayment, and when the mortgage clears. Use for 'how much equity will we have in 10 years'.

tools.name: calculate_pay_rise
tools.description: How much of a pay rise reaches take-home pay after tax, National Insurance, student loan and pension. Use for 'what is a £5,000 rise actually worth'.

tools.name: calculate_retirement_drawdown
tools.description: How long a pot lasts drawing a percentage of it in year one, rising with inflation, at a growth rate. A single path, not a simulation, so it gives no odds. Use for 'how long would £400k last at 4%'.

tools.name: calculate_dividend_drawing
tools.description: For a limited company director: how much retained profit can be drawn as dividends this tax year before the higher rate, the dividend tax on it, and what drawing it all costs, band by band. Use for 'how much can I take out of my company this year?'.

tools.name: calculate_tax_reserve
tools.description: For a sole trader: the share of each invoice to set aside for Self Assessment, this year's income tax and Class 4 NI bill, the 31 January and 31 July payments, and whether a reserve covers the next one. Use for 'how much should I put aside for tax?'.

tools.name: calculate_trade_vat
tools.description: For a builder, plumber, electrician or other trade: the VAT on one building job and who pays it (the domestic reverse charge), what CIS takes off, what is paid to them, and what they keep on standard VAT against the Flat Rate Scheme, plus whether their sales mean they must register for VAT. Use for

tools.name: calculate_capital_allowances
tools.description: For a limited company buying equipment, machinery or a van: how much of the cost comes off this year's profit (Annual Investment Allowance, full expensing, the 50% first-year allowance or writing down), the Corporation Tax that saves, and the same cost written down instead. Not for cars. Use for 'ho

tools.name: calculate_home_and_mileage
tools.description: For a sole trader: HMRC's flat rates for working from home and business miles against the business share of the real costs, and which claims more for each. Use for 'should I claim the flat rate for working from home?' or 'what can I claim for my business miles?'.

tools.name: calculate_protection_check
tools.description: The life and income cover a household would need if one earner died or couldn't work, against what it has: debts cleared and take-home pay replaced for a number of years, minus life cover, death in service and savings; and the monthly bills that pay covers, minus sick pay and income protection, with

tools.name: calculate_compound_growth
tools.description: What a starting sum plus a monthly amount grows to at an annual rate (as an AER) over a number of years, and how much of that is growth. Can also say how often interest is added, pay in at the start of each month, raise the monthly amount each year, or work backwards from a target: the monthly amoun

tools.name: calculate_fee_cost
tools.description: What a yearly percentage fee costs over the years: the same savings grown with and without the fee. Use for 'what does a 1% fee cost me over 25 years'.

tools.name: calculate_emergency_fund
tools.description: How many months of essential spending the Emergency fund calculator's rules point to for a household, the target in pounds, and how many months current savings would cover. Use for 'how big should my emergency fund be'.

tools.name: calculate_net_worth_by_age
tools.description: How a net worth compares with the typical (median) household wealth for that age band in the ONS Wealth and Assets Survey, and what share of all households in Great Britain (any age) have less. Use for 'is £150k good for a 40-year-old'.

tools.name: calculate_salary_vs_dividends
tools.description: For a limited company owner: what a salary and dividend split leaves after Corporation Tax, NI and personal tax, and the salary that leaves the most. Use for 'what salary should I pay myself from my company'.

tools.name: calculate_redundancy_pay
tools.description: The tax-free first £30,000 of a redundancy payment, the income tax on the rest given the year's other income, and what is received. Use for 'how much tax on a £45k redundancy payment'.

tools.name: calculate_ir35
tools.description: The same contract taxed inside IR35, as a deemed employee, against outside, run through the contractor's own limited company at the best salary and dividend split. Use for 'what's the difference inside IR35 on £90k'.

tools.name: calculate_self_employed_tax
tools.description: A sole trader's income tax and Class 4 NI from turnover and expenses (or the £1,000 trading allowance, if larger), what is kept, and next year's payments on account. Use for 'how much tax on £40k of self-employed income'.

tools.name: calculate_year_tax_owed
tools.description: This tax year's income tax, Class 4 NI and High Income Child Benefit Charge on pay, self-employment, rent, interest and dividends, less what PAYE has taken - whether a Self Assessment bill is coming, how much, whether a return is needed, and next year's payments on account. Use for 'will I have a ta

tools.name: calculate_sole_trader_vs_ltd
tools.description: The same trading profit kept as a sole trader against taken from a limited company at the best salary and dividend split. Use for 'would I keep more as a limited company'.

tools.name: calculate_house_affordability
tools.description: One run for a home purchase: stamp duty, the deposit with a Lifetime ISA (and its charge if the home is over the limit), the loan against what a lender's income multiple allows, and the monthly payment. Use for 'can we afford a £350k house'.

tools.name: calculate_remortgage
tools.description: Two remortgage deals over the length of the fix, fees included: the monthly payments, the total, and the tracker rate at which both cost the same. Use for 'should I fix at 4.3% or take a tracker at 4.6%' - the figures, not a recommendation.

tools.name: calculate_mortgage_repayments
tools.description: The monthly payment on a mortgage, repayment or interest-only, the total paid and the total interest, with what's still owed year by year. Use for 'what's the monthly payment on £250k at 4.5% over 25 years'.

tools.name: calculate_downsizing
tools.description: What moving to a cheaper home actually frees up, after selling costs, the mortgage, stamp duty and buying costs. Use for 'how much would we free up selling at £600k and buying at £400k'.

tools.name: calculate_gift_aid
tools.description: What a charity receives from a Gift Aid donation, what the donor can claim back at a higher rate, and what the gift really costs. Use for 'what does a £100 donation cost a higher-rate taxpayer'.

tools.name: calculate_company_car_tax
tools.description: The taxable benefit on a company car from its list price and CO2 figure, and the income tax it adds a year and a month. Use for 'how much tax on an electric company car worth £45k'.

tools.name: calculate_annual_allowance_taper
tools.description: The pension annual allowance once threshold income passes £200,000: whether it tapers, the reduced allowance, and how far contributions are over it. Use for 'how much can I pay into my pension on £280k'.

tools.name: calculate_lisa_withdrawal
tools.description: What taking money out of a Lifetime ISA early really costs: the 25% charge, and how much of it is the person's own money rather than the bonus. Use for 'what do I lose taking £4,000 out of my LISA'.

tools.name: calculate_seven_year_gifts
tools.description: Which lifetime gifts still count for inheritance tax, when each drops out, how much of the nil-rate band they use, and the tax on them if death were today. Use for 'we gave our son £50k in 2022 - does it still count'.

tools.name: calculate_career_break
tools.description: What a career break costs: pay given up, pension contributions missed, and what those contributions would have grown to by retirement. Use for 'what does a year off cost my pension'.

tools.name: calculate_state_pension_top_up
tools.description: Whether buying missing National Insurance years adds to the State Pension, what it costs, and how long it takes to pay back. Use for 'is it worth buying two missing NI years'.

tools.name: calculate_tax_code
tools.description: What a tax code on a payslip means - its tax-free pay, whether it's an emergency code - and, given a salary, the tax it takes against the standard code. Use for 'what does 1257L M1 mean', 'is my tax code right'.

tools.name: calculate_let_property_tax
tools.description: The yearly tax on a let property: profit on top of other income, the 20% finance-cost credit for mortgage interest (24% from 2027/28) (Section 24), or the £1,000 property allowance if better. Use for 'how much tax on my buy-to-let rent'.

tools.name: calculate_mortgage_stress_test
tools.description: A repayment mortgage's payment at today's rate and at one, two and 3 points higher, what each leaves of take-home once the bills and other debts are paid, the rate at which it would stop fitting, and the payment once a fixed rate ends. Use for 'what if rates went up 3%', 'could we still afford the m

tools.name: calculate_bonus_sacrifice
tools.description: A bonus taken as cash against some of it paid into the pension instead, over the whole year: what reaches the pocket either way once the £100,000 line, the childcare that stops there and the Child Benefit charge are counted, and the sacrifice that brings the year back under each line. Use for 'shoul

tools.name: calculate_ev_salary_sacrifice
tools.description: What a car through an employer's salary sacrifice scheme really costs a month: the take-home given up plus company car tax on its benefit, against leasing the same car privately. Use for 'is an electric car through salary sacrifice worth it', 'what does a £450 a month EV scheme cost me'.

tools.name: calculate_salary_for_take_home
tools.description: The salary before tax needed to take home a set amount a month or a year, after income tax, National Insurance, student loan and pension, at this tax year's rates - the take-home calculator's own sums, so the two agree to the pound. Use for 'what do I need to earn to take home £3,000 a month'.

tools.name: calculate_parental_pay
tools.description: Statutory Maternity, Paternity and Shared Parental Pay from usual pay before tax, week by week, with any employer top-up of full pay then half pay: the total, each week's pay, and how far short of usual pay it falls. Use for 'what will I get on maternity leave on £35k', 'how much is paternity pay'.

tools.name: calculate_making_tax_digital
tools.description: Whether Making Tax Digital for Income Tax applies to a sole trader or landlord, and from when - qualifying income (self-employment and property income before expenses) over £50,000, £30,000 or £20,000 - with the first year's quarterly update and tax return dates. Use for 'do I need Making Tax Digita

tools.name: calculate_car_finance
tools.description: The same car over the same term, compared as PCP (keeping it or handing it back), hire purchase, leasing and cash: the monthly payment, the total each costs, the interest in it, and what is owned at the end. Only the ways given are shown. Use for 'PCP or HP on a £25k car', 'is leasing cheaper than b

tools.name: calculate_premium_bonds
tools.description: What a typical (median) year of Premium Bond prizes is on an amount - most holders win less than the prize fund rate - against a savings account's interest after tax, and the savings rate that beats it. Use for 'are Premium Bonds worth it on £20k', 'what savings rate beats Premium Bonds'.

tools.name: calculate_balance_transfer
tools.description: Moving a card balance to a 0% balance transfer offer: the fee, the monthly payment that clears it before the 0% ends, what's left when it ends at a given payment and what that then costs, and the saving against staying on the card it's on now. Use for 'is a 0% balance transfer worth it on £4,000', '

tools.name: calculate_junior_isa_vs_sipp
tools.description: The same money paid in each year for a child until 18, into a Junior ISA and into a Junior SIPP with its basic-rate tax relief, grown at the same rate: the pot at 18 and at the minimum pension age, and when the child can get each. Use for 'Junior ISA or Junior SIPP for my daughter', 'what would £2,8

tools.description: An interactive Retirement Planner: their pension pot year by year to 100, in today's money, with sliders for the age they retire, what they pay in a month and what they spend a year, and the State Pension from their State Pension age. Starts from their own pensions and Retirement overview figures, w

tools.name: get_mortgage_overpayment_planner

tools.description: An interactive ISA Allowance Planner: what's left of this tax year's ISA allowance, with a slider for what they'd pay in each month until 5 April and what would be left then - and, for someone with a Lifetime ISA, the part of it going there and the government bonus it adds. tools.description: An interactive Budget View: the Budget page drawn in the chat - take-home, the bills, debt payments and saving that come off it, what's free each month, where the bills go by category, how long their cash would last, and what's coming up. The same figures as the Budget page. Use for 'show me my budg

tools.name: get_goals_tracker
tools.description: An interactive Goals Tracker: every savings goal drawn in the chat with its progress bar, target year, whether it's on track and what a month would close any gap. The same figures as the Goals page. Use for 'show me my goals', 'how are my goals doing'.

tools.name: get_tax_year_end_check
tools.description: Before the tax year ends: every allowance they haven't used yet this tax year - ISA, Lifetime ISA, pension and carry-forward, Capital Gains Tax, dividends and each child's Junior ISA - with the pounds at stake, which kind (allowance lost, bonus lost, tax saved later, tax due), and the date to act by

tools.name: get_budget_changes
tools.description: Every tax change already announced in a Budget for later tax years, run on their own figures: what each costs or saves them a year (savings and dividend tax rates, allowances, pensions counting for inheritance tax, the salary sacrifice NI cap), by the tax year it starts in, biggest first, and the re

tools.name: get_regions
tools.description: Their investments split by region - US, UK, Europe, Asia, emerging markets and global - in pounds and as a share of all their investments, with the biggest holdings in each, their own share of joint accounts, and a global fund split by its factsheet where one is added. The same split as the Region c

tools.name: get_employer_shares
tools.description: Their employer share grants - RSUs, EMI, CSOP and unapproved options, Sharesave and Share Incentive Plans - each with how much has vested and how much is still to vest, in shares and pounds at today's price, the next vest date and amount, and when the whole grant has vested. The same figures as Empl

tools.description: Foliopeak's own plain-English explanation of a UK money topic - an account type, a tax rule, a strategy - with a link to the full article. Use when someone asks what something is or how a rule works.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_attention, get_report, list_notifications, get_monthly_review, get_budget_view, get_goals_tracker · Private data: get_cairn_history, get_business, get_career_break_cost · Public sink: get_holdings, get_report, get_resilience, calculate_pension_carry_forward, calculate_tax_reserve, calculate_home_and_mileage, calculate_net_worth_by_age, get_tax_year_end_check, get_regions, get_employer_shares · Destructive: calculate_ir35, calculate_house_affordability, get_budget_changes.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_attention, get_report, list_notifications, get_monthly_review, get_budget_view, get_goals_tracker · Private data: get_cairn_history, get_business, get_career_break_cost · Public sink: get_holdings, get_report, get_resilience, calculate_pension_carry_forward, calculate_tax_reserve, calculate_home_and_mileage, calculate_net_worth_by_age, get_tax_year_end_check, get_regions, get_employer_shares · Destructive: calculate_ir35, calculate_house_affordability, get_budget_changes

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
